_comment: Ledger of recurring prose habits (constructions, gestures, paragraph/scene closers), the language-level counterpart to motifs.json. Nightly sessions read this before drafting and add entries after. Status: 'develop' = use only in a new form; 'rest' = do not use until rested_until chapter; 'watch' = fine in moderation. Saturday review prunes and logs counts.

constructions.pattern: 'the way [clause]' used as a trailing simile
constructions.example: the way you feel an old break in the weather before you feel the ache of it
constructions.note: Zero again in ch. 16, a delirium chapter built almost entirely out of manner-clause comparisons (the stairs, the voices, the courteous man) that was drafted with several 'the way X' constructions and had every one of them rewritten to a plain 'as' clause or cut, same remedy as ch. 15. Demoting to rest as flagged last time — five of the last six chapters at zero or one. Leave this construction alone for a real stretch; the plain-'as' replacement is doing the work now.

constructions.example: a thing to explain; a thing your body has quietly decided
constructions.note: Seventh chapter running at zero, including ch. 16, where a vague placeholder noun would have been the easy way to gesture at everything delirium left unnamed and wasn't reached for even once. Safe to consider this one fully retired rather than merely resting.

constructions.pattern: 'I have learned/found/never...' followed by a general rule
constructions.example: I have learned the exact weight a thing has to reach before it's worth the cost of saying it out loud
constructions.note: Seventh chapter running at zero. A draft pass of ch. 16 produced a near-miss ('is, I have come to understand, a different skill altogether') in the Ivet beat and it was cut back to a plain statement with no self-aware hedge. Stays on watch rather than retired, since the delirium register makes this one easy to slip back into.

Ch. 16 at 19, same band held through a whole-chapter unreliable-narration experiment. Contrast partner rotated to its most minimal form yet: Lloyd's long, overlapping delirium sentences pulled up short by Maria's bare grounding words reaching him from outside the slide (cup. window. blanket. her own hand.) rather than by another character's combat calls or institutional paperwork. Keep rotating into ch. 17, where the contrast partner should probably become physical nursing detail rather than dialogue at all.

constructions.pattern: 'same as [clause]' used as a trailing comparison, the direct replacement for the rested the-way-simile
constructions.example: same as I run all of them back now
constructions.note: Four chapters running at exactly one use (Maria's hand on his chest, 'the same as I had every single time since the chapel'). Settled, controlled background usage — no change in status.

constructions.pattern: Lloyd narrates his own perception-management in filing/accounting/procedural language
constructions.example: filed and closed and not brought up again; I did the sum; running the frame back
constructions.note: Sixth chapter running clean. Ch. 16 was the strongest possible temptation for this one — a whole chapter of Lloyd trying to manage facts he can't otherwise process, including the knot-cord count — and it still reached for arithmetic as a dry joke rather than filing language. Treat as effectively retired.

constructions.pattern: a clause restated through its own negation for flat understatement — 'didn't X because there wasn't X to do', 'wasn't an answer that wasn't Y'
constructions.example: she didn't say anything useful, because there wasn't anything useful to say; I didn't have an answer that wasn't the same thing said back to her, worse
constructions.note: Sixth chapter running without it. Not reached for in ch. 16 either, despite several places (the buried memory, the cord) where a negated restatement would have been an easy shape to default to; still safe to use if it arises naturally, not a default.

constructions.pattern: a statement capped with a trailing 'which was/is [flat judgment]' clause
constructions.example: which was true, and also the kindest thing she could have said to her just then; which was as much of a question as Edie generally asks
constructions.note: Four chapters clean now. A draft pass of ch. 16's opening produced one bare trailing 'which told me...' close and it was split into two short declaratives instead, same remedy as ch. 12-13. Treat any return to the bare trailing-'which' shape as a real lapse.

closers.pattern: paragraph or chapter ends on the narrator stating what he did not say, or what the scene means
closers.example: I said none of that. I hadn't said anything since the school wall and didn't start now.
closers.note: Ch. 15 and ch. 16 both avoid it. Ch. 16 ends on a bare image — daylight through the gap in the Callow Ford roof, mid-slide, no resolving line and nothing stated about what it means — which is the chapter's own outline requirement (no lucid interval, no final clarity) as much as it is this ledger's preference. Three chapters (12-14) still the longest run on this pattern; neither ch. 15 nor ch. 16 is added to the chapters list.

closers.pattern: chapter ends on an image of something indifferent or inanimate personified as 'patient', waiting out time without hurry
closers.example: the night came down slow over the burnt manse... patient, working at the dark the way it works at everything, given enough time and no one to tell it to stop
closers.note: Spent at ch. 08-09 review; stayed spent through ch. 13. Do not return to 'patient' as a chapter-ending word.
